extracted.intended_audience: regulatory analysts, economists, stakeholders (businesses and consumer advocates) participating in FTC notice-and-comment on negative-option/click-to-cancel rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Economic and compliance-cost methodology and assumptions used to estimate benefits and costs of the FTC final rule on cancellation mechanisms for negative-option subscriptions (click-to-cancel). Intended to inform rulemaking and public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of consumers' time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission values consumers' non-market time at $25.81 per hour (2023 dollars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to monetize time costs of cancellation attempts (e.g., one minute of time equals $0.43). This wage-rate valuation is applied when estimating per-cancellation and total consumer benefits from reduced time burdens under the final Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worst-case gym membership cancellation scenario
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes three failed cancellation attempts, each costing one hour, resulting in three unwanted monthly charges processed, and a fourth attempt (one hour) that succeeds in halting recurring payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined with consumer time valuation and typical gym monthly fees ($40–$70) to compute a high-end per-cancellation cost in the absence of the Rule: (4 × $25.81) + (3 × $70) = $313.25. With final Rule allowing ≤1 minute to cancel (value $0.43), avoided burden = $312.82. This scenario is a simplifying assumption for high-end estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-cancellation benefit categories and ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Four per-cancellation benefit scenarios with low and high estimates: phone→online; online→simpler online; phone→simpler phone; in-person→online or phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated per-cancellation benefit ranges (2023 dollars): phone→online: $2.17–$2.39; online→simpler online: $0.46–$0.67; phone→simpler phone: $1.74–$2.17; in-person→online or phone: $0.46–$312.82. These are applied to counts of cancellations by baseline method to compute total benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer population baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'consumers' for analysis as the U.S. population age 18 and over, estimated at 269 million in 2025 (Year 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This population baseline is used to scale subscription prevalence and total subscription counts over the 10-year evaluation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription prevalence and per-subscriber subscriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes 83% of American consumers have at least one subscription and the average subscriber has 4.5 subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied multiplicatively (.83 × adult population × 4.5) to estimate the aggregate number of subscriptions per year (e.g., Year 1: .83 × 269M × 4.5 = ~1,004.72 million subscriptions). Notes uncertainty: household/shared subscriptions or future growth could bias estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Churn rate/time-dimension caution and annualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses a voluntary churn rate of 3% per month, assumed constant month-to-month and year-to-year, yielding an annual churn rate of 36%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit caution that churn rates reported without a time dimension can be misinterpreted; treating a monthly rate as annual would vastly misstate cancellations. The 36% annual rate is multiplied by subscriptions to estimate annual cancellations (e.g., Year 1: 36% × 1,004.72M = 361.70M cancellations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy for in-person subscriptions (gym memberships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses gym membership prevalence as a proxy for subscriptions entered into in person: 19% of U.S. population are gym/health-club members, producing 51.11 million adult gym members (Year 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies IHRSA 2019 annual attrition rate (28.6%) to estimate gym cancellations as a proxy for in-person subscription cancellations (Year 1: 14.62M). Acknowledges limitations (other in-person subscription types excluded; age distribution and shared family memberships may bias estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline distribution of cancellation methods from enforcement matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on review of 54 FTC matters meeting criteria, the baseline distribution for subscriptions entered online/phone is: 66.7% offered online enrollment + telephone cancellation (36/54); 11.1% offered online enrollment + online cancellation (6/54); 22.2% offered telephone enrollment + telephone cancellation (12/54).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extrapolates these shares to the national sample to estimate numbers of cancellations by baseline method (e.g., Year 1: 231.39M phone cancellations of subscriptions entered online; 38.56M online cancellations of subscriptions entered online; 77.13M telephone cancellations of telephone-entered subscriptions). Notes potential bias: enforcement matter sample may overweight problematic practices and assume no baseline compliance with the new Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping baseline cancellation categories to final Rule outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes that under the final Rule: subscriptions enrolled online & cancelled by phone will move to online cancellations; enrolled online & cancelled online will move to simpler online cancellation; enrolled by phone & cancelled by phone will move to simpler telephone cancellation; in-person enrollments will allow online or phone cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mapping is used to assign the appropriate per-cancellation benefit range to each baseline cancellation count when aggregating benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total benefits aggregation and discounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Total benefits are computed by multiplying the number of cancellations in each baseline category by the matched per-cancellation benefit (low and high), summing across categories, and discounting over 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a 2% discount rate over a 10-year horizon to compute present discounted value (PDV) and annualized benefits. Example estimates: Year 1 benefits range $661.52M–$5.32B; PDV over 10 years at 2%: $6.13B–$49.32B; annualized: $682.83M–$5.49B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universe of firms for compliance-cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes 106,000 firms offer negative option plans and will need to take some actions to comply with the final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance costs (familiarization, disclosure changes, cancellation mechanism changes, recordkeeping) are estimated across this universe. Data limitations in comments required reliance on external studies and proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarization cost assumptions (hours and wage proxies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopts U.K. Impact Assessment survey hours: senior staff 4–16 hours; service staff 0–80 hours. Proxies: senior staff→attorneys at $84.84/hr; service staff→average of salespersons & clerical workers at $23.27/hr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to all 106,000 firms to estimate aggregate initial-year familiarization costs between $35.97M and $341.22M. No commenters provided firm-specific estimates so UK data used as analog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure-change cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes for online marketers covered by ROSCA, required disclosure changes are textual only (no architecture changes) and can be performed by web developers at $45.95/hr in 1–10 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-firm disclosure compliance range: $45.95–$459.50. Assumes some firms already compliant (18.75% of online firms) and therefore incur no incremental disclosure costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rule minimum cancellation-mechanism requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketers must provide a simple cancellation mechanism in the same medium and at least as simple as the mechanism used to obtain consent, with additional medium-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive electronic medium: cancellation must be easy to find (not hidden in terms & conditions) and cannot require interactions with live/virtual representatives if consent did not require such interactions. Telephone: telephonic cancellation must be available during normal business hours and not more costly to consumers than the telephone call used to consent. In-person consent: marketers must offer cancellation opportunities where practical in a like manner and must offer an alternative simple cancellation method via interactive electronic medium or by providing a telephone number that satisfies the Rule's telephone requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental evidence-based segmentation of online sellers and remediation assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Uses UK experimental research on 16 online subscription sellers to segment compliance needs: 18.75% offered easy online cancellation (<1 minute), 62.5% had non-intuitive labeling requiring relabeling, 18.75% offered only telephonic cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes 18.75% need no website change; 62.5% can comply via relabeling (no programming) at 1–8 hours of a web developer ($45.95/hr); 18.75% that offered only telephonic cancellation may need to build online cancellation at estimated costs $0–$532.05 per firm (2023 dollars), acknowledging many platforms/processors offer free tools. These percentages are extrapolated from online-only sample to full firm universe due to data limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relabeling cost bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For sites that need only to relabel navigation/links (e.g., change 'auto-renew' or 'edit plan' to 'unsubscribe'/'cancel'), assume 1–8 hours of web developer time at $45.95/hr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-firm relabeling cost range: $45.95 (1 hour) to $367.60 (8 hours). The Commission treats the U.K. 8-hour estimate as an upper bound even if cosmetic changes might require less time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration (click-to-cancel) cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: For firms offering only telephonic cancellation but having online ordering architecture, estimated cost to integrate simple click-to-cancel tools ranges between $0 and $532.05 per firm (2023 dollars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate based on external (OuterBox) 2022 cost approximations updated to 2023 dollars; recognizes payment processors or hosting platforms may provide tools at no incremental cost to many firms. No commenter data on build vs. third-party usage existed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of telemarketers in cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's prior estimate is that 2,000 of the 106,000 firms are telemarketers. Because telemarketers control call length and cancellation flow, the Commission assumes telemarketers face no incremental cancellation-compliance costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid downward bias, the Commission nevertheless does not exclude the 2,000 telemarketers from the denominator when computing aggregate costs, but it assumes no incremental telemarketer-specific cancellation costs absent data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA cost estimates (information collection burden) are a subset of total compliance costs. The Rule's recordkeeping costs are estimated separately at $6.54 million aggregated across firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes commenters conflated PRA estimates with total compliance costs. The total-cost estimate includes familiarization, disclosure, mechanism changes, and recordkeeping; PRA-only estimates understate total compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-year and ongoing compliance cost aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial-year costs sum familiarization, disclosure, cancellation-mechanism changes, and recordkeeping. Ongoing (years 2–10) compliance costs are assumed to be minimal for disclosures and cancellation mechanisms because templates can be reused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial-year estimated aggregate range: $49.52M–$422.26M (2023 dollars). Ongoing costs: once compliant templates exist, adding/changing products uses the template and is treated as routine business cost rather than incremental compliance cost; thus no additional ongoing compliance costs are assumed for disclosures/cancellation mechanisms beyond recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of data limitations and sensitivity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Where comment record lacked specific data (e.g., distribution of enrollment/cancellation methods, firm-level costs), the Commission relies on proxies (UK studies, enforcement matters, external estimates) and acknowledges these limitations may bias estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission explicitly notes potential over- or under-estimation sources (e.g., enforcement sample weighting, household-shared subscriptions, unknown number of firms already compliant) and conducts sensitivity analyses elsewhere in the rule economic analysis to explore impacts of these limitations.
